scope: Static reverse engineering; no sample was executed on the host. Unicorn emulated only the DEW extraction/decryption routine with memory-only API stubs.

samples.marker_line: Arvion loader: ETW patching and debugger hiding; add evasion rules
evidence: Unsigned x64 image with SpeechRuntime version resources and an encrypted overlay occupying most of the file; internal ARVION/Arvion markers identify the loader, not a verified malware family.
WinMain at 0x140001fc0 creates a single-instance mutex and launches a hidden /speechrt watchdog; its normal path calls the loader at 0x1400044e0.
The loader calls initialization at 0x140025c70 (call sites 0x14000455f, 0x140004622, 0x1400046a9). This hashes EtwEventWrite and EtwEventWriteFull, resolves ntdll exports, and calls 0x140029610.

The patch helper changes the target page to writable/executable, saves the original byte, writes 0xc3 at 0x1400296f4, and restores page protection. This suppresses ETW function execution rather than implementing speech features.

0x14000b9b0 invokes NtSetInformationThread with class 0x11 and null information/length, via generated native syscall stubs with a resolver fallback. Calls occur in the early initialization at 0x140026068 and 0x14002607b.
0x14000b140 generates MOV R10,RCX; MOV EAX,service-number; JMP [RIP+0] and the target pointer. This is a neutral syscall capability; its intent comes from the separate ETW/thread-hiding paths.

CopyFileW installation paths under Microsoft app-data directories and HKCU Run-key writes are visible at 0x140005304 onward and 0x14000591d onward. The watchdog and system-style names corroborate concealed durable loading.

Overlay acquisition/reconstruction is implemented in 0x140015a30, called from 0x14000eed9; it processes encrypted chunks, expands runs, copies output chunks into the assembled buffer, and clears intermediate buffers. Final payload identity and runtime delivery success were not established here.
samples.verdict_balance: ETW suppression, debugger hiding, concealed payload reconstruction and watchdog installation outweigh the claimed speech-runtime purpose. No authorized deployment context or trustworthy publisher signature was supplied.

samples.identification: DEW custom loader carrying a Telegram RAT
samples.marker_line: DEW loader: concealed Telegram RAT and keylogger; fix KEM false match
evidence: Unsigned MinGW x64 wrapper, zero PE timestamp, no Authenticode signature or authoritative product identity. Its dominant .reloc section contains a-p nibble words wrapped in a misleading Microsoft schema/manifest comment.

WinMain 0x140005780 first calls 0x140001570. That gate rejects one-or-fewer processors, RAM below 1536 MiB, screen dimensions below 640x480 and very low color depth; unrelated UI calls sit behind an implausible screen-width branch.
The normal path runs the installation helper 0x140002640, the extraction/decryption helper 0x140004de0, and the manual image mapper 0x140004870.

0x140004de0 parses the final section, locates encoded delimiters, decodes alphabetic Base16 pairs into bytes, unmasks a header, and calls the ChaCha implementation at 0x1400017c0; it validates the recovered payload with CRC32.

Unicorn extraction reproduced the helper, producing 1086976 bytes with SHA256 bc330096abb1481ac51e7e3d91d98728ffae16c5ce6ab98c06b739c11364d14b. Both the encrypted intermediate and recovered PE are retained in the scratch directory.

The mapper allocates a local image, copies sections, resolves imports, applies relocations (types 3 and 10), sets protections, calls TLS callbacks, and invokes AddressOfEntryPoint at 0x140004c1b. It does not establish remote-process injection.

FNV-1a export-name lookup at 0x1400014c0 obtains native functions without readable import names. OneDriveTelemetrySync and OneDriveHealthHelper path fragments support the masquerading installation helper.

The recovered payload contains api.telegram.org, a hardcoded bot credential (redacted), getUpdates polling, and update_id parsing. The polling routine 0x1400129f0 uses the HTTP helper 0x140003990; the task dispatcher calls the command runner at 0x1400125e5.

The command runner 0x140006740 creates an inheritable pipe, builds cmd.exe /C plus the supplied command, launches it hidden using CreateProcessW at 0x1400069cd, and captures output with ReadFile at 0x140006a6f. The dispatcher sends the result back through 0x140008310.

The keyboard callback 0x14000e3c0 handles key-down messages, obtains foreground-window titles, checks modifier state, converts keys with ToUnicodeEx, records input in a shared buffer and handles clipboard paste. The initialization installs this callback (0x14000eeb4). No execution or successful data theft was assumed.
Runtime names also include a DDoS handler and browser-extension installation material; those untraced capabilities were not used to manufacture hostile rules or family attribution.

The KEM decapsulation finding was false: the matched text kemigbmpokdecapj is a random word in the a-p encoded payload, not a KEM routine. The observed payload cipher is ChaCha. The matcher now permits numeric suffixes/separators instead of arbitrary intervening letters.
samples.verdict_balance: A concealed and configured remote-command/keylogging payload, hidden command execution, installation camouflage and analysis gates establish malware. The malware-corpus provenance corroborates but does not decide this judgement.

samples.identification: Chinese Element Client game-automation bot with MicroSu CAPTCHA helper
samples.marker_line: ElementClient bot: game automation; no covert theft found; keep traits
evidence: Unsigned x86 E-language application; Chinese UI data refers to the Wulin/Element Client game, automatic combat, HP/MP controls, quests, parties, inventory filtering and multi-account operation. This is a game bot/cheat, not a verified official game component.
The file is already reconstructed: UPX0 contains populated code/data and imports are rebuilt in .imports. upx -d reports NotPackedException. UPX section labels alone do not prove active unpacking.

PhysicalDrive0 access at 0x4041d1 opens a device and calls DeviceIoControl with IOCTL_STORAGE_QUERY_PROPERTY (0x2d1400). It obtains device properties/serial material; no destructive disk-write path was found. The existing notable create/write co-occurrence profile is accurately worded and retained.

Game-process memory access, remote-thread API references, window automation, hooks and code-patch helpers agree with the bot purpose. These dual-use capabilities remain detected. The sandbox showed a near-identical helper image launched under a configuration directory and memory written into that child; this does not by itself establish a remote backdoor.

A startup path at 0x4202d5 tests the availability of the external-IP page and can call 0x4209ab. That routine uses hardcoded SMTP account/recipient settings to send results of 0x420bad as subject/body. 0x420bad fetches and extracts the public IP from ip138.com; the reviewed email path did not include game passwords or local documents. This telemetry is a concern, but public-IP reporting alone did not establish malicious theft.

The embedded MicroSu.dll at file offset 0x20210f is a 61440-byte VB6 COM CAPTCHA-solving client. It provides SendImage/GetAnswer/Report and user/card/account operations; strings and COM/HTTP method paths implement image/form upload and answer polling at su.microrui.com and su2.microrui.com. File/image transfer capability is retained rather than relabeled as malware.

The actual Triage behavioral report flags rebuilt UPX material, a dropped helper, read-only physical-drive access, host/locale discovery, hooks and a parent-to-child WriteProcessMemory event. The analyzed run crashed and reported no TCP/UDP requests. That runtime limit is not evidence of benign intent.

Forager retrieved the IP lookup URL, which now redirects to a DNS/IP lookup site; the content was an ordinary lookup page. Both MicroSu hosts and the ecodeproject developer forum failed DNS resolution after retries. eyuyan.com resolves to the E-language vendor site. Historical CAPTCHA service responses therefore could not be verified.

No independent covert credential/document theft, malicious remote tasking, destructive action, or substitute malware payload was established in the reviewed execution paths or bundled DLL. The heuristic source label is plausibly driven by the recovered UPX layout, process modification and raw-device inspection.
samples.verdict_balance: The observed bot and CAPTCHA workflows explain its intrusive capabilities, while the SMTP path transfers public-IP information rather than credentials. Authorization, original distribution history and historical service responses remain unknown. BENIGN is the requested balance-of-evidence judgement for sighted quarantine, not a clean upstream attestation.

trait_severity_rationale: The outer binary profiles establish probable ETW patching, debugger hiding, encoded-payload concealment and analysis gates, at suspicious severity. Each malicious input has two distinct suspicious findings. More aggressive hostile family/credential-theft claims would exceed those static matchers; no duplicate or unsupported rules were added to reach hostile counts.

retained_controls: Real liboqs 0.14.0 kem.h fetched with provenance: KEM decapsulation and usage findings unchanged.
Existing testdata/hostile/flashhole/lpeclient_reconstruction.c: both hostile detections and all old findings retained.
Existing testdata/hostile/flashhole/lpeclient_variant.py: both hostile detections and all old findings retained.
Existing kem-public-key.py capability near miss: all old findings retained.
coverage_preservation.network_severity: GetAdaptersInfo textual API reference promoted from component to notable; matcher and supported coverage unchanged.

remaining_gaps: ML still returns benign/class 0/level -1 for both independently verified malicious loaders despite suspicious rules. Do not restore the false KEM finding to alter this score.
The recovered DEW payload is not automatically extracted by the normal outer-file pipeline; analysis of its manual recovered PE also underflags the RAT.
The third sample remains high-probability in the raw model despite the benign dual-use judgement; both gates are benign. All 68 findings on embedded MicroSu.dll and 336 on its parent were retained.
The first loader final payload was not independently recovered or attributed. The second was recovered and traced; no runtime success was inferred.

validation_fixture_review.initial_failure: Only two does-nothing fixture views rejected the promoted GetAdaptersInfo textual reference.
validation_fixture_review.evidence: testdata/does-nothing/main.go only initializes and flushes klog and logs a message. The compiled Windows fixture contains the complete GetAdaptersInfo API name, so the reference observation is accurate.
validation_fixture_review.fix: Allow this exact notable trait in the two existing Windows Go fixture overrides. Preserve the matcher, severity, score caps and every forbidden/attack expectation. No rule downgrade or Go-wide suppressor was added.
